clue.text: Well, a bacillus you can count on

definitions.text: Well, a bacillus you can count on

parts.words: Well, a bacillus you can count on
parts.note: the clue plays on the sound of 'a bacillus': a germ you can count with, read as a bead frame used for doing sums

explanation.surface: A microbiologist muses on one reliable germ.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'a bac-' of 'a bacillus' leads into a counting frame with beads; 'count on' is literal, meaning to do arithmetic with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead frame is a device people literally count on when doing arithmetic.

clue.text: Vigorous new plant

parts.note: a yellow-flowered shrub, and the saying that a new one sweeps clean, said of an energetic newcomer

explanation.surface: A gardener admires a strong young seedling.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'a new broom sweeps clean' is about a fresh appointee eager to change things; the word is also a yellow-flowered shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered shrub, whose name also appears in a proverb about energetic newcomers sweeping clean.

clue.text: Lead us in an ancient melody

parts.note: to conduct is to lead or direct
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to be guided through an old tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval Latin song set to music, sung in processions, is an old tune.

clue.text: Ignoramus finally joining the elite? Very funny

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the cream is the best, the elite

explanation.surface: Sarcasm at a fool trying to join high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hilarious is described as a riot or a hoot, very funny indeed.

clue.text: Disorders in the skin the Scholar Gypsy was familiar with

definitions.text: the Scholar Gypsy was familiar with

indicators.note: the disorders are placed inside the skin, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a skin of an animal is its hide
disorders are ills, ailments

explanation.surface: Skin complaints that a famous wandering figure knew well.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scholar Gypsy is the wanderer of Matthew Arnold's Victorian poem, who roamed the slopes and hills around Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Arnold's poem has its scholar roaming the rising ground above the Thames near Cumnor, a sloping country landscape he knew well.

clue.text: Standard tools you would 26, say

parts.note: a flag showing two tools; 26 is the phrase meaning assume, which sounds like 'take as red', red being the communist colour

explanation.surface: Equipment one might simply assume to be standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' means a flag, here the Soviet one; 26 across, said aloud, suggests 'take as Red', since red stands for communism.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet flag showed a crossed mallet and reaping blade, emblem of workers and peasants.

clue.text: Hang on to one chance at last in the slips

parts.note: to linger is to hang on, stay around
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Advice to cling to a final chance while fielding in the slips at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slips' suggests the cricket fielding position, but here means petticoats and underslips.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips are petticoat-style undergarments, a type of women's underwear.

clue.text: Old city's singular doom — eruption

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: an eruption throws things about, so the letters of doom are scattered

explanation.surface: An ancient city meets a unique fate in a volcanic eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city destroyed with Gomorrah is an old city.

clue.text: Seamstress's unfinished task?

parts.note: a needlework with threads pulled from the fabric; a game left level is also called drawn, as if unfinished

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's half-done job.
explanation.walkthrough: A drawn match ends with no winner, as if left unfinished; the needlework uses threads drawn out of the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornamental needlework made by pulling threads out of cloth is a seamstress's craft.

clue.text: Fellow-Englishman, but not from London?

definitions.meaning: a compatriot, someone from the same nation as you
a rural dweller, someone from outside the capital and towns

explanation.surface: Someone from the same nation who happens to live outside the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a compatriot and a person who lives in rural parts rather than the city.

clue.text: This port is a bargain

definitions.meaning: a harbour town on the Kent coast in England
an agreement struck between two parties

explanation.surface: A harbour town offered as a good buy.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAL is a small town on the Kent coast of south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the English Channel coast, and also a transaction or agreement struck between parties.

clue.text: Carve off joint, set out mat — eat up!

indicators.note: set out means the letters of the following words are laid out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A carving instruction at the dinner table: cut the joint, lay the mat, tuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges MAT, EAT and UP; 'joint' looks like a roast but is part of the definition, a limb joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut off a limb at a joint is the surgical operation of removing it.

clue.text: I may belong to Earl, but King belongs to me

parts.note: ER is the abbreviation for Edward Rex, a king
something that belongs to me is mine

explanation.surface: A robe boasting that it may be an earl's property but the monarch is its own.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the fur itself: white winter stoat fur trims the robes of peers such as earls.
explanation.definitionFit: The white winter fur of the stoat trims the ceremonial robes worn by peers.

clue.text: Extract from' a traditional passage

indicators.note: an extract is a piece drawn out of something, so the answer is taken from within the next word

explanation.surface: A passage quoted from an old traditional text.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after 'from' is a printing speck. 'Extract from' takes the run inside traditional.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal entrance tunnel into a mine is a kind of underground passage.

clue.text: Italian cathedral admits form of dice — small book may be made

indicators.note: admits means the cathedral lets the other letters inside it

parts.note: duomo is the Italian word for a cathedral

indicators.note: form of means the letters of dice are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A small book could be made about dice games in an Italian church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges DICE into DECI, which goes inside DUOMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A book size made by folding each sheet into twelve leaves gives a small volume.

clue.text: Cartoonist can be enlivening

definitions.meaning: a person who draws moving cartoon films
in Latin the word is one who gives life, so something that is enlivening; the clue's 'can be' links the two senses

explanation.surface: A remark that a cartoon artist can liven things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon film maker brings drawings to life, and the Latin root means one who gives life.

clue.text: Cats learn to be wild, or is it inherited?

indicators.note: to be wild means the letters of the two words run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A question of whether feline wildness is learned or innate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something passed down from forebears is inherited.

clue.text: Madly brave boy? One's very words

indicators.note: madly means the letters of brave are jumbled

parts.note: Tim is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A remark about a crazily courageous lad, quoted exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoting someone word for word gives exactly the speaker's own phrasing.

clue.text: Shoots elephant, perhaps, with antique piece

parts.note: pots, as in takes a pot shot, means shoots
elephants gather in a herd, so the animal hints at its group

explanation.surface: A big-game hunter bags an elephant along with an old artefact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots' reads as a noun, new growth, but is the verb: to pot game is to shoot it.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken fragment of ancient pottery found by archaeologists is a piece from antiquity.

clue.text: Go hard with a sponge perhaps

definitions.meaning: to become encrusted and hardened, as mud does
a sponge is one kind of baked sweet treat

explanation.surface: Advice to scrub firmly with a bath sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: Mud will set into a hard crust, and a Victoria sponge is a sweet baked dessert.

clue.text: The romance of business

definitions.meaning: a matter or concern, as in 'that is my business'

explanation.surface: Love as something businesslike.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a love liaison and a matter or concern to be dealt with.

clue.text: Plaster and litter — beginnings of an urban blight

parts.note: a litter is a stretcher or bed for carrying

indicators.note: beginnings of takes the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Rubbish and graffiti cover a run-down part of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' suggests rubbish but means a bed or straw bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear something thickly over a surface is to plaster it.

clue.text: An attempt to cause embarrassment

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
to have a bash is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: A try at making someone blush.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone feel ashamed or disconcerted is to embarrass them.

clue.text: Popular blend for a cuppa

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
a fusion is a blend of things

explanation.surface: A fashionable tea mixture for your daily brew.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is made by steeping leaves in hot water, the steeped drink being a cup of tea.

clue.text: No change of egg supplier

parts.note: O, a zero, means nothing or no
to vary is to change

explanation.surface: A constant source of eggs, as on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: The female reproductive organ produces the ova, so it supplies eggs.

clue.text: When talking, the prophet produces sparkling material

indicators.note: when talking means the prophet's name is said aloud and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: Micah is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: An Old Testament seer whose sermons yield something glittering.
explanation.definitionFit: A glittering silicate mineral that splits into thin shiny flakes is a sparkling material.

clue.text: Dispense with formality for a minute

definitions.text: Dispense with formality for a minute

parts.words: Dispense with formality for a minute
parts.note: at a meeting the record of the last one is often accepted without being read out; 'minute' is that record, not a moment

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes the rules briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like a short time but means a written record of a meeting, which committees often approve without reading aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming something without examining it is what committees do with the record of a previous meeting.

clue.text: Part of America in prosperity — that's good cheer

indicators.note: in places the American state inside the word for prosperity

parts.note: a boom is a time of prosperity
NH is the abbreviation for New Hampshire, a US state
IE stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Economic good times in one US region bring a cheerful mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly geniality and good nature amount to good cheer.

clue.text: Sets out again for the races

definitions.meaning: lays out once more, as with a table or carpet
team races in which runners take turns

explanation.surface: A punter heads off once more for a day at the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out something a second time, and team races run in stages with batons passed.
